svg.title: How attend decides when an event wakes the agent
svg.desc: A small machine on a bench, read left to right. Events arrive on a belt and pile up in a glass hopper that is one window for one scope. A gate under the hopper opens when an act ends, after a 500 millisecond grace for a closing event or at once for a message to the agent. The batch rides a tray to a dial gauge, the judge, whose needle swings to one of six routes: wait, skip, ask, note, queue or interrupt. Six chutes carry the batch to an agent at a desk. Wait loops the batch back up to the hopper, skip drops into a bin, and only interrupt rings the bell and lights the lamp.
